title: Strain-controlled magnetism and magnetoelasticity in monolayer NiPS$_3$ and CrPS$_4$
authors: Balázs Nagyfalusi, Alvaro Bermejillo-Seco, Linde de Jong, Ritesh Das, Yaroslav M. Blanter, Herre S. J. van der Zant, Amador Garcia-Fuente, and Jaime Ferrer
abstract: We develop a first-principles framework for magnetoelastic coupling in two-dimensional magnets based on a strain-dependent Heisenberg model. In this approach, strain derivatives of the exchange interactions provide direct access to magnetostriction and to the magnetic renormalization of the elastic tensor, establishing a microscopic link between spin interactions and elastic response. We apply the method to monolayer NiPS$_3$ and CrPS$_4$, which exhibit contrasting magnetoelastic behavior. NiPS$_3$ shows weak and nearly isotropic spin-lattice coupling, consistent with a robust zigzag antiferromagnetic ground state. In contrast, CrPS$_4$ displays strong anisotropic coupling, leading to strain-driven transitions between spin-spiral and ferromagnetic phases and significant changes in the critical temperature and elastic response. Our results demonstrate a general route to quantify magnetoelastic effects in low-dimensional magnets and highlight CrPS$_4$ as a promising platform for strain engineering of magnetic order.
summary: This paper establishes a comprehensive first-principles framework to quantify magnetoelastic coupling in 2D magnets using strain derivatives of exchange interactions. By applying this method to $	ext{NiPS}_3$ and $	ext{CrPS}_4$, the authors demonstrate that while both materials show magnetostriction, $	ext{CrPS}_4$ exhibits significantly stronger, anisotropic coupling, allowing external strain to robustly control its magnetic phase transitions.
main_problem: The study develops a first-principles framework to microscopically link spin interactions (magnetism) with elastic response (lattice structure) by quantifying magnetoelastic coupling in 2D magnets.
main_result: The work distinguishes between two regimes: $	ext{NiPS}_3$ shows weak, isotropic coupling, while $	ext{CrPS}_4$ exhibits strong, anisotropic coupling that allows strain to drive transitions between different magnetic phases (e.g., spin-spiral to ferromagnetic).
method: Calculations use DFT to derive strain derivatives of exchange interactions, which are then incorporated into a strain-dependent Heisenberg model solved via Monte Carlo simulations.
model_or_system: The system involves monolayer magnets ($	ext{NiPS}_3$ and $	ext{CrPS}_4$) modeled by a strain-dependent Heisenberg Hamiltonian. The total elastic energy is expanded to second order in strain, incorporating magnetic contributions derived from exchange coupling changes.
key_observables: Magnetostriction, renormalization of the elastic tensor ($A_{ij}$), critical temperatures ($T_c$), and the stability/phase diagram of magnetic ground states (FM vs. SS).
important_parameters: Strain ($\varepsilon$), Hubbard $U$ correction in DFT, and the magnitude of exchange couplings ($J_{ij}$).
main_assumptions: The derivation retains only the leading contribution from isotropic exchange interactions; calculations are performed assuming a fixed monolayer thickness.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate possible unit cell deformations under strain, show magnetic phase diagrams mapping ground states vs. applied strain ($\varepsilon_x, \varepsilon_y$), and plot $T_c$ dependence on strain.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from developing the general theory of magnetoelastic coupling (Section I), detailing the DFT/MC computational methods for both electronic structure and elasticity (Section II), before applying this unified framework to analyze $	ext{NiPS}_3$ and $	ext{CrPS}_4$ separately.
why_interesting: The explicit, quantitative link between lattice strain and magnetic phase transitions is highly relevant. Understanding how external mechanical stress can tune quantum ground states or critical temperatures provides a pathway for designing novel spintronic devices.
